name: Almon W. Babbitt
role: Church agent and lawyer rebuked in section 124
dateNote: He was appointed president of the Kirtland stake in October 1840; section 124 rebukes him in January 1841.
importance: Section 124 says he set up his own counsel instead of the First Presidency’s and compares this to a golden calf. Historians link this to his urging Saints to stay at Kirtland rather than gather to Nauvoo. He was restored and later led at Ramus and served as a Church trustee in 1846. He was disciplined several times, excommunicated in 1854, and killed on the plains in 1856.
connections: He married Julia Ann Johnson in 1833. He worked under Joseph Smith and later Brigham Young, and became secretary of Utah Territory in 1852.

sources.title: Almon Whiting Babbitt, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born Oct. 1812, Cheshire, Massachusetts; Camp of Israel 1834; Seventy 1835; Kirtland stake president 3 Oct. 1840; disfellowshipped 1835, 1840–1841, 1849, 1851; Ramus presiding elder 1843; trustee 1846; excommunicated May 1854; killed at Ash Hollow. JSP gives no death date. Wikipedia gives 9 Oct. 1812 and death by Cheyenne attack in 1856 (it lists c. 7 Sept. 1856 but also mentions August), so the day is uncertain. The Kirtland explanation of 124:84 is Wikipedia’s, marked as likely.
